note: The guild's camp on the BARE plate (1536x1024, no painted people, no baked speech).
Coordinates are plate pixels, read off game/assets/bg/stage_camp.png itself and
checked with `python tools/art/preview_scene.py stage_camp`.
figure_scale 2 (W1-STAGE, STAGE-02): the plate's own tents are ~210px and its crates
~35px, so a person is ~75-90px — twice the 31-48px strips. Every actor without its own
`scale` is drawn at this scale; the bubbles below hang over the 2x heads (an entry is the
kit's 40x44 emote frame's top-left: x = feet.x - 6 puts the tail's apex on the head's centre
line, y = feet - 2*frame_h - 44 - 6 puts that apex 6px above the head; the same rule places
the 1x tavern and market bubbles) and the actors are spaced so no two 2x bodies overlap by
more than a quarter. TOWN-07 moved the rogue and the brown variant out from under the
Tavern and Market callouts (numbers are 1x-era; W2-TOWN re-measures the callouts).
Bubbles (W2-STAGE2, TOWN-26): a third entry is an emote key from the icon grid — the
warrior sweats over the stew pot, the knight by the tents has a question, the figure at the
beds hums, the cleric dozes by the fire (zzz); the ranger says "...". Three of those five
are up at a time (`bubble_visible` 3) so ANY pick shows two glyphs — the Town shot's
acceptance is "at least two glyph bubbles" and a seeded 2-of-5 pick could show one (the
W2-STAGE2 review did). The skull over the bridge figure carries a MOOD (fourth
entry, "wipe"): it is up only while the screen has called `set_mood("wipe")` after a
lost raid. `speech.speaker` is a LIST: the line's hash picks its mouth among figures that
carry no bubble and stand under no callout — cleric_b by the tents, mage_b at the top.
The lanterns are LIGHTS plus a 6x8 FLAME each (W4-LIFE, TOWN-27, spec 09 §5 rank 2):
this plate is top-down and its lanterns are 8-12px, so the 16x24 fire strip would be
bigger than the lamp; `flame_lantern.png` (gen_fire.lua, 3 frames at 8 fps) is the
dedicated strip that row asks for, and each `props` entry below sits on a painted
flame measured as the warm-bright blob nearest its light (the light positions are
the glow's centre, 5-10px off the glass), with a per-instance `phase`. The campfire
is the one fire big enough for its own sprite, and it sits on the painted flame so
the static one is covered rather than doubled.
W4-LIFE, motion on paths: `paths` sends two townsfolk walking the open dirt — one along the
band between the Town's Blacksmith plate (plate x 556..946, y 462..542 on the Town's framing)
and its Board plate (606..846, 638..712), short of the pines at (680+, 600+); one up and down
the grass left of the quartermaster's crates, under the speech plate's foot (y 532) — a 2x
body is 78 px tall, so the strolls are short: no walker passes under a callout — on the walk strips
gen_actors.py derived (`<who>_walk`), turning back at each end; the north and west
banners are `props` cut from this plate's own pennants (banner_wave / banner_wave_b,
opaque crops anchored `topleft` at their origin, frame 0 = the plate) that ripple at
the hem. All held by SceneStage.apply_settings under reduced_motion.
Twelve figures, because the camp is the guild's home and a raid is twelve. They
are placed where a camp gives someone something to do: the fire ring, the stew
pot, the vegetable beds, the quartermaster's table, the tent mouths, the bridge.
spec 09 §5 row 4's water, on the river down the right cliff and the stream under the
bridge — the two places this plate paints moving water and then holds it still.

lines: I think I'm ready for a real raid this time!
Has anyone seen my other boot?
The tank said left. I heard right.
Do we still get paid if we run?
I read the strategy. Most of it.
Nobody said there would be fire.
I'm not lost. The dungeon is.
